summary: Half Moon Bay sits on the Pacific side of the Santa Cruz Mountains, which means the only way in or out by car is Highway 1 along the coast or Highway 92 over a winding, fog-prone mountain pass — a geographic bottleneck that keeps the town feeling remarkably isolated despite being just 28 miles south of San Francisco. That isolation is the defining fact of daily life here: the coastside bluffs deliver unobstructed sunset-over-ocean views and direct access to miles of coastal trails and state beaches, but the tradeoff is a commute over 92 to Silicon Valley employers that can stretch past an hour when weather or a single fender-bender closes a lane. With a median home price near $1.47 million against a median household income of roughly $153,000, the price-to-income ratio lands around 9.6× — steep even by Bay Area standards, and monthly rent at $2,299 reflects a market shaped more by scarcity of buildable land than by local job density. The town itself is compact at 6.3 square miles with a walkable Main Street anchored by independent restaurants, a few coffee shops, and the famous annual pumpkin festival and farmers' market, but daily errands beyond groceries often require a drive. Year-round highs average just 64°F with remarkably narrow temperature swings, meaning summer fog replaces what most Californians expect to be sunshine season. Half Moon Bay is essentially a coastal village tethered to a major metro by a single mountain road — and that road shapes nearly every practical decision about living here.
